data.title: Were large soda lakes the cradle of life?
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了磷元素在生命起源中的关键作用，以及大型苏打湖（如美国加州的莫诺湖）可能是生命起源的摇篮。磷是DNA、RNA和ATP等重要分子的组成部分，但在地表较为稀缺。研究表明，生命起源前的化学反应需要极高浓度的磷，而大型无外流苏打湖通过蒸发保持磷浓度，满足了这一条件。这些湖泊由于水体蒸发，磷无法被冲走，从而积累到足够浓度，支持生命起源的化学反应。与小湖不同，大湖的磷供应足够持久，能维持生命的发展。因此，研究人员认为，大型苏打湖可能是生命起源的理想环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同环境下的生命起源理论，特别是碱性湖泊和碱性热液喷口与生命起源的关系。

不同观点：
• **[culi]** 认为高碱性湖泊是高生产力的生态系统，尽管适应这种极端环境的生物被视为“嗜极生物”，但也许我们这些不生活在极端环境中的生物才是真正的“嗜极生物”。他指出，在生态学中，“生产力”通常通过测量系统中的生物量增长速率来确定。

• **[gomijacogeo]** 分享了一个关于科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的Harry Brodsky讨论海洋喷口周围磷可用性的视频，将讨论引向海洋喷口和磷元素对生命起源的重要性。

• **[Sniffnoy]** 质疑磷的可用性是否是碱性湖泊作为生命起源地的唯一原因，并将其与生命起源于碱性热液喷口的理论进行比较，提醒大家碱性热液喷口与著名的“黑烟囱”不同。

• **[BobbyTables2]** 以幽默的方式提问碱性湖泊是否有电解质，属于轻松的插曲，没有提出实质性论据。

• **[m0llusk]** 支持碱性湖泊环境可能为早期生命提供条件的说法，并进一步提出地下通道和空腔也可能为早期生命提供了环境。这些地方有高温、丰富的矿物质（包括磷），以及各种相互连接的空腔，可以作为反应室甚至细胞。

• **[toast0]** 引用他人观点，戏谑地指出富含磷的大型苏打湖可能是生命起源的地方，并用可乐作比喻，继续围绕磷元素的作用展开讨论。

• **[im3w1l]** 引用了被标记为“无意义”的评论，质疑关于生命起源的推测是否有价值。他认为这种推测可以为未来的研究提供方向，如寻找早期生命的遗迹或在实验室中模拟生命起源的条件。如果这些研究有希望，可以为外星生物学提供线索，并影响未来探测器的发射方向。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于关于生命起源的推测是否具有科学价值以及如何验证这些推测。im3w1l等人认为这些推测难以验证，但也有观点认为这种推测可以指导未来的实验和探索。
• 讨论中多次提到磷元素在生命起源中的重要性，以及不同环境（碱性湖泊、碱性热液喷口、地下空腔）作为生命起源地的可能性。

Were large soda lakes the cradle of life?
Geochemistry and Petrology
Research
Life needs sufficient phosphorus. However, the element is scarce, not only today but also at the time of the origin of life. So where was there sufficient phosphorus four billion years ago for life to emerge? A team of origin-of-life researchers has an answer.
25.03.2025
by
Peter Rüegg, Corporate Communications
volume_up
Read
mode_comment
Number of comments
In closed soda lakes, such as Mono Lake in California, phosphorus accumulates to such an extent that it triggers prebiotic chemistry. (Image: Rikk Flohr / AdobeStock)
In brief
Phosphorus is a key molecule for life, but the element is relatively rare on Earth.
However, a very high concentration of phosphorus was necessary to set the first chemical reactions in motion that preceded life and led to the formation of important molecules such as RNA.
Large, phosphorus-rich soda lakes are the most likely places to have met this requirement. Researchers believe that it was in such lakes that prebiotic chemistry began and life emerged.
Along with nitrogen and carbon, phosphorus is an essential element for life on Earth. It is a central component of molecules such as DNA and RNA, which serve to transmit and store genetic information, and ATP (adenosine triphosphate), which cells need to produce energy.
Phosphorus may also have played a key role in the origin of life. Certain conditions are needed to trigger the start of the biochemical processes that precede life. One of these is the presence of sufficient phosphorus. Its availability regulates the growth and activities of organisms. Unlike nitrogen or carbon, however, phosphorus is relatively rare at Earth's surface – which was the case in the era before life existed as well as today.
It is precisely because phosphorus is rare and so difficult to obtain, yet subject to high demand by living organisms, that scientists have long wondered how life could have arisen at all.
To answer this question, they conducted experiments in the laboratory. These showed that prebiotic chemistry requires very high concentrations of phosphorus – about 10,000 times more phosphorus than naturally occurs in water. This raises the question of how and where such high concentrations of phosphorus in water occurred on Earth billions of years ago.
Earth scientist Craig Walton has a new answer: large soda lakes without natural runoff could maintain phosphorus concentrations for a sufficiently long time, even if life begins to exist in them at some point (and continuously consumes phosphorus). The results of the study have just been published in the journal
Science Advances
.
Such lakes lose water only through evaporation. This means that phosphorus is left in the water instead of being washed away through rivers and streams. As a result, very high concentrations of phosphorus can build up in these soda lakes.
As early as 2020, researchers from the University of Washington had suggested that soda lakes could be the cradle of life. Walton has now taken this further. The researcher is investigating questions about the origin of life from a geochemical perspective as part of a Nomis fellowship at ETH Zurich’s
Centre for
Origin and Prevalence of Life
(COPL).
Not every soda lake is suitable; Walton excludes small ones. “As soon as life develops in them, their phosphorus supply would be depleted faster than it is replenished. This would nip in the bud both the chemical reactions and the developing life,” says Walton. In large soda lakes, on the other hand, the phosphorus concentrations are high enough to sustain both the basic chemical reactions and life over the long term. These high concentrations are achieved through a high volume of inflowing river water, which contains phosphorus, while water only leaves the lake through evaporation. Since phosphorus does not evaporate easily, it stays behind and accumulates in the lake.
One example of such a large soda lake is Mono Lake in California. It is about twice the size of Lake Zurich. In Mono Lake, the phosphorus concentration remains constantly high, allowing a wide variety of organisms to flourish. This is crucial because in small lakes, the phosphorus is used up before new amounts can be
formed.
Phosphorus in Mono Lake is therefore maintained at a high concentration, which means that a lot of phosphorus regularly flows in without the phosphorus content dropping too quickly.
Walton and his team therefore consider large soda lakes that had a constant high phosphorus supply in the early history of the Earth to have been an ideal environment for the origin of life. The researchers assume that life is more likely to have originated in such large bodies of water than in small pools, as Charles Darwin had suspected.

data.title: Show HN: macOS app to reduce eye strain (open-source)
data.author: Remy42
data.article_summary: BlinkMoreFree 是一款开源的macOS菜单栏应用，旨在通过屏幕褪色和自动眼动追踪技术，提醒用户多眨眼以减轻眼睛疲劳。应用使用Mac内置前置摄像头进行眼动追踪，并确保隐私安全，数据不会离开设备。该应用有免费版和高级版，高级版可根据使用的应用程序智能开启或关闭眼动追踪，适合阅读等文本密集型任务。使用时需确保摄像头能清晰看到眼睛，并注意设备角度以获得最佳体验。应用由oxremy和AI共同开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款应用的开发、功能建议、技术要求及其实际效果

不同观点：
• opan指出该项目缺乏明确的许可证文件，并建议开发者选择合适的开源许可证。这是一个关于项目合法性和开源策略的技术性问题。

• thisislife2对开发者选择绕过App Store发布应用表示赞赏，并提出三点建议：1) 支持旧版macOS以扩大兼容性；2) 参考类似软件如Workrave和Timeout进行功能改进；3) 认为Workrave在功能上优于Timeout，建议开发者多关注Workrave。这是一个关于功能扩展和竞争分析的建设性反馈。

• pimlottc对应用的核心功能提出质疑，认为人体自然的眨眼频率已经足够保护眼睛，暗示该应用可能没有实际必要。这是一个对应用实际效果的怀疑观点。

• cududa对该应用表示赞赏，并表示有兴趣深入了解和尝试使用。这是一个积极的支持性评论。

• MelodyUwU对应用要求macOS Sonoma表示担忧，认为该技术要求过高，可能限制用户使用。这是一个关于技术门槛的反馈。

• pcdoodle支持该应用的想法，并进一步建议添加一个提醒用户注视远处以锻炼眼睛焦距的功能，这是一个功能扩展建议，旨在进一步保护眼睛健康。

• MichaelTheGeek简单表示该应用的想法很好，是一个简短的支持性评论。

补充讨论：
• 关于许可证的合法性问题（opan）
• 对macOS版本兼容性的关注（thisislife2, MelodyUwU）
• 对应用核心功能的科学性质疑（pimlottc）
• 功能扩展和竞争分析（thisislife2, pcdoodle）
• 对项目整体的积极反馈（cududa, MichaelTheGeek）

争议焦点：
• 应用的核心功能是否必要，特别是人体自然眨眼是否足够保护眼睛（pimlottc的质疑与其他支持性评论之间的对比）。

总体来看，讨论围绕应用的技术实现、功能建议及其科学性展开，既有积极反馈也有建设性批评。

BlinkMoreFree
BlinkMoreFree is an open source macOS menu bar application that helps reduce eye strain by fading your screen when you stare at it for too long without blinking. Using automated eye-tracking and customized settings to encourage you to blink more.
BlinkMore
If you like the free version consider
BlinkMore
. Main difference: eye tracking turns on/off based on the app you are using, saving energy by only turning on for apps you choose. I like to use with text-heavy tasks like reading/research.
Requirements
macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later
Uses Mac's built-in front facing camera
Privacy
Everything happens right on your Mac—no data leaves your device or sticks around after you close the app. No accounts or personal information needed.
Tips for Best Experience
Make sure your Mac's camera has a clear view of your eyes (heads-up: glasses at certain angles may have reflections that obstruct camera view).
Consider the angle of your camera. Blink detection may not work at extreme angles, like laying in bed with Mac on your lap.
BlinkMoreFree is perfect for text-heavy tasks like reading––just know it uses a good chunk of your Mac's power.

data.title: Deciphering language processing in the human brain through LLM representations
data.author: Korling
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人类大脑在日常对话中如何处理自然语言，并与大型语言模型（LLMs）的处理方式进行比较。研究表明，LLMs通过自监督学习目标（如下一词预测）和强化学习生成上下文相关的语言输出，其内部表示（嵌入）与人类大脑处理语言时的神经活动呈现线性对应关系。研究使用侵入性电极记录人脑神经活动，并与Whisper语音转文本模型的嵌入进行比较，发现模型中的语音嵌入与大脑语音区（如颞上回，STG）活动对应，语言嵌入与语言区（如布罗卡区，Broca's area）活动对应。在语言理解和生成过程中，模型嵌入能准确预测神经响应的时序，揭示了LLMs在理解人脑语言处理机制方面的潜力。研究发表在《Nature Human Behaviour》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）与人类大脑在语言处理和内部表征上的比较

不同观点：
• fernly认为原作内容难以理解，尤其是对“embedding”一词的使用表示质疑。他们指出，将LLM的内部结构直接与大脑内部结构进行比较是高度可疑的，因为人类语言模型明显依赖于符号化的语法和句法规则，而LLM则不依赖。
• namaria则认为相关研究非常有趣，但指出这些研究基于非常小的实验对象群体，且结论强调LLM仅仅是回显输入统计数据，并不能像人类一样思考和理解。
• cs702持相反观点，认为当前模型不仅仅是“随机鹦鹉”，因为它们学习和建模世界的方式与人类大脑有相似之处，尤其是通过线性变换对齐大脑和LLM的embedding。
• Ey7NFZ3P0nzAe提出问题，是否存在某种定理可以解释随机few-hot向量的线性组合能匹配任何信号，并对LLM与脑信号匹配的趋势表示关注。
• probably_wrong怀疑这些研究仅仅展示了脑活动与Transformer模型之间的相关性，而从相关性推导到本质相同的结论是过于牵强的。
• teabee89对研究中的500ms延迟表示不满，认为如果能预测人的思想会更有说服力。
• macleginn指出使用OpenAI模型进行研究的讽刺性，同时提到之前使用GPT-2进行类似研究的连续性。
• ggm认同研究结果，认为神经活动与LLM在语言生成上的序列模式存在相似性，尤其是在将思想序列化以产生语言的过程中。
• taosx对研究表示赞赏，并期待更多关于大脑的发现，希望能更好地理解和“破解”大脑。
• ogogmad则进一步推测这种研究是否能帮助实现大脑上传以达到永生。

Deciphering language processing in the human brain through LLM representations
March 21, 2025
Mariano Schain, Software Engineer, and Ariel Goldstein, Visiting Researcher, Google Research
Large Language Models (LLMs) optimized for predicting subsequent utterances and adapting to tasks using contextual embeddings can process natural language at a level close to human proficiency. This study shows that neural activity in the human brain aligns linearly with the internal contextual embeddings of speech and language within large language models (LLMs) as they process everyday conversations.
Quick links
Paper
Share
Copy link
×
How does the human brain process natural language during everyday conversations? Theoretically, large language models (LLMs) and symbolic psycholinguistic models of human language provide a fundamentally different computational framework for coding natural language. Large language models do not depend on symbolic parts of speech or syntactic rules. Instead, they utilize simple self-supervised objectives, such as next-word prediction and generation enhanced by
reinforcement learning
. This allows them to produce context-specific linguistic outputs drawn from real-world text corpora, effectively encoding the statistical structure of natural speech (sounds) and language (words) into a multidimensional embedding space.
Inspired by the success of LLMs, our team at Google Research, in collaboration with
Princeton University
,
NYU
, and
HUJI
, sought to explore the similarities and differences in how the human brain and deep language models process natural language to achieve their remarkable capabilities. Through a series of studies over the past five years, we explored the similarity between the internal representations (embeddings) of specific deep learning models and human brain neural activity during natural free-flowing conversations, demonstrating the power of deep language model’s embeddings to act as a framework for understanding how the human brain processes language. We demonstrate that the word-level internal embeddings generated by deep language models align with the neural activity patterns in established brain regions associated with speech comprehension and production in the human brain.
Similar embedding-based representations of language.
Our most
recent study
, published in
Nature Human Behaviour
, investigated the alignment between the internal representations in a Transformer-based speech-to-text model and the neural processing sequence in the human brain during real-life conversations. In the study, we analyzed neural activity recorded using
intracranial electrodes
during spontaneous conversations. We compared patterns of neural activity with the internal representations — embeddings — generated by the
Whisper
speech-to-text model, focusing on how the model's linguistic features aligned with the brain's natural speech processing.
For every word heard (during speech comprehension) or spoken (during speech production), two types of embeddings were extracted from the speech-to-text model —
speech
embeddings from the model’s speech encoder and word-based
language
embeddings from the model's decoder. A linear transformation was estimated to predict the brain’s neural signals from the speech-to-text embeddings for each word in each conversation. The study revealed a remarkable alignment between the neural activity in the human brain's speech areas and the model's speech embeddings and between the neural activity in the brain’s language area and the model's language embeddings. Broca’s area
(located in the

43439501.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人类大脑在日常对话中如何处理自然语言，并与大型语言模型（LLMs）的处理方式进行比较。研究表明，LLMs通过自监督学习目标（如下一词预测）和强化学习生成上下文相关的语言输出，其内部表示（嵌入）与人类大脑处理语言时的神经活动呈现线性对应关系。研究使用侵入性电极记录人脑神经活动，并与Whisper语音转文本模型的嵌入进行比较，发现模型中的语音嵌入与大脑语音区（如颞上回，STG）活动对应，语言嵌入与语言区（如布罗卡区，Broca's area）活动对应。在语言理解和生成过程中，模型嵌入能准确预测神经响应的时序，揭示了LLMs在理解人脑语言处理机制方面的潜力。研究发表在《Nature Human Behaviour》上。

data.title: We're Still Not Done with Jesus
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了耶稣的生平及其历史背景，以及基督教如何从他死后兴起的过程。文章提到耶稣作为犹太拉比和殉道者，其追随者创立了以他为“基督”的宗教。耶稣与佛陀、穆罕默德并列为三大宗教创始人。文章重点讨论了伊莱恩·佩格尔斯的著作《奇迹与奇事》，她研究了耶稣生平和早期基督教文献，包括圣保罗书信和四部福音书。这些文献的来源和真实性存在不确定性，福音书在耶稣受难后四到六十年用希腊文写成，作者并非目击者。文章还提到耶稣的处女 birth 故事可能是为了回应当时质疑而引入的，此类神迹在希腊罗马文化中并不罕见。早期基督教与异教神话存在相似之处，这也被一些学者重新评估。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章中关于《福音书》和早期基督教历史观点的批评与分析

不同观点：
• **Ninjinka** 认为文章中关于《福音书》作者不可能是目击者的说法不准确。他指出，希腊语在当时是东罗马帝国的通用语言，耶稣及其门徒可能懂希腊语。此外，他认为马太和约翰作为十二使徒之一，有可能是目击者。
• **throw0101c** 反驳文章对早期基督徒动机的质疑。他认为早期基督徒在传播信仰时面临迫害，并没有实际利益可得，因此他们的行为不应被简单视为文学创作或神话构建。
• **room271** 认为文章具有论战性质，缺乏对学术共识的探讨。他指出文章旨在解释宗教的持久性，但缺乏深度分析，很多论点没有充分论证。
• **drekipus** 质疑文章中将耶稣称为“拉比”的合适性，并指出耶稣后来被犹太教视为异端。不过，他赞赏耶稣的教义使基督教更具包容性。
• **ggm** 提到历史学中关于人物如大流士或凯撒存在的证据问题，指出《福音书》文本的编辑历史复杂，并认为早期基督徒因被迫害而未能系统整理“目击者”记录。
• **Reasoning** 对文章中的一些具体例子提出质疑，如用普鲁塔克的作品来比较《福音书》中的神性孕育故事，认为时间线和文化背景不同使这种比较不恰当。他还对《福音书》是否完全脱离口述传统表示怀疑。
• **corkybeta** 提到文章中提及理查德·卡里尔（Richard Carrier）的神话论角度不值得讨论，并认为蒂姆·奥尼尔（Tim O'Neill）对卡里尔的反驳更为可取。

补充讨论：
• **KerbalNo15** 引用《哥林多前书》和《罗马书》的内容，强调基督教信仰的核心信息和持久性，指出宗教信仰不应被简单地视作历史或文学现象。

争议焦点：
• 文章中关于《福音书》作者是否为目击者、希腊语的使用、以及《福音书》是否基于口述传统的论述引发讨论。这些讨论主要围绕历史准确性和文章例子的恰当性。
• 对早期基督徒动机的理解和《福音书》创作背景的不同解释也是争议的焦点，尤其是关于历史证据和宗教信仰之间的关系。

One subject that never dies, and, more significantly, never bores, is the life and times of the first-century Jewish rabbi and martyr Jesus, whose followers founded a religion in his name, or, rather, in honor of his title, Christ, meaning “the anointed one,” or Messiah. (Not necessarily a divine title, it had previously been associated with military and religious leaders, often indicating something closer to “the great” than “the godlike.”) Along with Buddha and Muhammad, he is one of three nameable figures credited with founding religions that have continued to grow over thousands of years.
The Princeton professor emeritus Elaine Pagels, who has written many imposing and engrossing books on early Christianity, is back with a kind of culminating work, “
Miracles and Wonder
” (Doubleday), the title slyly looking at both St. Paul and Paul Simon. Though her purposes are manifold, she begins by ably navigating through the shoals of the essential but surprisingly unsettled sources that seem to relate the events of Jesus’ life and death. There are, first, the Epistles of St. Paul, the late convert who brought the Jewish heresy to the Gentiles, releasing it from Torah observance and law, and making it a universal faith. The seven undisputed Pauline letters were written in and around the fifties, about fifteen to twenty years after the Passion; six others are regarded as later, polemical forgeries, correcting Paul’s egalitarianism with more gender-bound rules. Then, there are the “letters” (Hebrews and Jude and so on) of uncertain early date and more uncertain authorship.
Most important, there are the four Gospels, written in Greek some forty to sixty years after the Crucifixion is thought to have happened. These were composed somewhere far from Jerusalem, in a language that Jesus and his disciples would not have known, by writers who could not have been eyewitnesses. The books are attributed, in probable order of composition, to Mark, Matthew, Luke, and John, with the attribution provided by the Greek formula of “according to,” unique to these texts. The suggestion is that these are not accounts “by” So-and-So but “the story as told to” So-and-So.
What We’re Reading
Discover notable new fiction, nonfiction, and poetry.
Though fugitive and fragmentary, the events in the Gospels take place on a fixed historical time line. Judea, the remaining Jewish kingdom—conquered throughout the centuries by Assyrians, Persians, and Greeks—was annexed by the Roman Empire around 6 C.E. The story of Jesus’ life, if accurately reported, occurred in the brief window between the annexation and the Jewish revolt of the sixties and seventies. That fanatic rebellion, mournfully chronicled by the great Jewish historian Josephus, ended in a catastrophe rivalled in the history of Jews only by the Holocaust; it involved the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem, the enslavement and exile of thousands, and the loss of sovereignty over Jewish holy sites. From this desolation arose the Messianic faith of Christianity, which, after the conversion of the Emperor Constantine in 312, eventually became the Roman Empire’s sole state religion.
How Jesus’ story fits into this framework is very much Pagels’s question. She’s working within a tradition of historical-Jesus studies that took shape in earnest more than two centuries ago, and for her the Gospels are palimpsests of lore, legend, and propaganda, beneath which a core of oral transmission and shared recollection remains detectable. The shifting Nativity narratives, for instance, suggest that rumors about Jesus’ parentage existed from the beginning. Pagels notes that the miraculous-birth stories appear relatively late. Paul—who never met Jesus, though he might have met his brother—mentions nothing about a virgin birth. Neither does Mark, who makes Jesus’ adoption by God as his son the true beginning of the story, tied to Jesus’ baptism by John. In various texts, including Apocryphal works that date to around the same time as the Gospels proper, Joseph appears to suspect Mary of infidelity. Meanwhile, an early Jewish polemic claimed that Jesus was the illegitimate son of a Roman soldier nicknamed Panther—perhaps employing a tasteless but pointed pun on the Greek word
parthenos
(virgin).
The story of the virgin birth, Pagels argues, was introduced by Matthew and, in another version, by Luke in order to address such lingering doubts. The consoling notion of divine impregnation was commonplace in the Hellenistic world, with countless tales of gods foisting demigods on virgins. Plutarch, for instance, described Rome’s founder Romulus as born to a divinely impregnated vestal virgin. As Catherine Nixey, a writer for
The Economist
, shows in “
Heretic: Jesus Christ and the Others Sons of God
” (Mariner), an irreverent reassessment of the Jesus stories in light of similar myths, early Christians didn’t merely acknowledge these parallels but

data.title: Scientists break down plastic using a simple, inexpensive catalyst and air
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 北西部大学的研究人员开发了一种简单且经济的方法，利用空气中的湿气分解塑料废物。该过程使用无毒、环保的无溶剂方法，通过廉价的催化剂分解聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）的键，然后暴露在空气中，借助空气中微量的湿气将分解的PET转化为单体，这些单体是塑料的重要 building blocks。该技术比当前的塑料回收方法更安全、清洁、便宜且可持续，为创造塑料的循环经济提供了有希望的途径。该研究已发表在《Green Chemistry》上，解决了塑料废物这一全球紧迫的环境挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料回收的技术、政策、成本及环境影响

不同观点：
• [piokoch] 认为塑料种类繁多，识别材料是回收的主要难题，且当前制度让公民和地方政府承担了回收成本。他建议强制使用单一塑料类型和易移除标签，并指出企业在包装材料选择上的自由导致了环境问题。
• [lxmorj] 提出通过完全燃烧一次性塑料来减少其长期环境影响，认为这样至少能得到两次使用价值，尽管这种方法并不理想。
• [culi] 关注回收技术的效果，尤其是分解成单体的比例和微塑料残留问题，并对当前技术能否解决不可回收塑料提出疑问。
• [vagab0nd] 认为塑料的难以降解特性实际上是其广泛使用的原因，提出任何"解决方案"可能会引发新的问题。
• [Synaesthesia] 强调政府法规的重要性，认为中国禁止一次性塑料是一个有效措施，并指出很多塑料使用是不必要的。
• [stosssik] 对新技术的前景持谨慎乐观态度，关注技术能否在避免专利垄断和集中 exploitation 的情况下发展。
• [wolfi1] 提到通过机械手段将PET瓶回收成食品级瓶子的可能性，指出已有欧洲公司提供这种机器。

补充讨论：
• [voidUpdate] 对新技术能否实际应用持怀疑态度，暗示很多创新技术最终不了了之。
• [kikokikokiko] 指出文章未提供该回收过程的最终成本估算，对实际经济可行性提出质疑。
• [kylehotchkiss] 对催化剂的简单性表示惊讶，暗示原以为会有更复杂的技术。
• [Xiol32] 担心塑料分解产物可能带来的健康风险，尤其是对人体的潜在影响。
• [whynotnowplz] 提出将垃圾扔进火山的极端处理方法，尽管这在实际操作中不切实际且危险。

• 塑料回收过程中识别材料的困难和成本分配不公是讨论的核心问题。piokoch主张强制使用单一材料和标签，而实际操作中的经济和技术可行性受到其他讨论者的质疑。
• 塑料处理方法的有效性和环境影响，如燃烧和分解技术的利弊，也是争议的重点。

Scientists break down plastic using a simple, inexpensive catalyst and air
by Amanda Morris,
Northwestern University
The photographs show the TPA product formation at different runs after every 4 h of heating (total reaction time = 20 h). Credit:
Green Chemistry
(2025). DOI: 10.1039/D4GC05916F
Harnessing moisture from air, Northwestern University chemists have developed a simple new method for breaking down plastic waste.
The non-toxic, environmentally friendly, solvent-free process first uses an inexpensive catalyst to break apart the bonds in polyethylene terephthalate (PET), the most common plastic in the polyester family. Then, the researchers merely expose the broken pieces to ambient air. Leveraging the trace amounts of moisture in air, the broken-down PET is converted into monomers—the crucial building blocks for plastics. From there, the researchers envision the monomers could be recycled into new PET products or other, more valuable materials.
Safer, cleaner, cheaper and more sustainable than current plastic recycling methods, the new technique offers a promising path toward creating a circular economy for plastics. The study was recently
published
in
Green Chemistry
.
"The U.S. is the number one plastic polluter per capita, and we only recycle 5% of those plastics," said Northwestern's Yosi Kratish, the study's co-corresponding author. "There is a dire need for better technologies that can process different types of
plastic waste
. Most of the technologies that we have today melt down
plastic bottles
and downcycle them into lower-quality products.
"What's particularly exciting about our research is that we harnessed moisture from air to break down the plastics, achieving an exceptionally clean and selective process. By recovering the monomers, which are the basic building blocks of PET, we can recycle or even upcycle them into more valuable materials."
"Our study offers a sustainable and efficient solution to one of the world's most pressing environmental challenges: plastic waste," said Naveen Malik, the study's first author. "Unlike traditional recycling methods, which often produce harmful byproducts like waste salts and require significant energy or chemical inputs, our approach uses a solvent-free process that relies on trace moisture from ambient air. This makes it not only environmentally friendly but also highly practical for real-world applications."
An expert in plastic recycling, Kratish is a research assistant professor of chemistry at Northwestern's Weinberg College of Arts and Sciences. Kratish co-led the study with Tobin J. Marks, the Charles E. and Emma H. Morrison Professor of Chemistry at Weinberg and a professor of materials science and engineering at Northwestern's McCormick School of Engineering. At the time of the research, Malik was an postdoctoral fellow in Marks' laboratory; now he is a research assistant professor at the SRM Institute of Science and Technology in India.
The plastic problem
Commonly used in food packaging and beverage bottles, PET plastics represent 12% of total plastics used globally. Because it does not break down easily, PET is a major contributor to plastic pollution. After use, it either ends up in landfills or, over time, degrades into tiny microplastics or nanoplastics, which often end up in wastewater and waterways.
Finding new ways to recycle plastic is a hot topic in research. But current methods to break down plastics require harsh conditions, including extremely high temperatures, intense energy and solvents, which generate toxic byproducts. The catalysts used in these reactions are also often expensive (like platinum and palladium) or toxic, creating even more harmful waste. Then, after the reaction is performed, researchers have to separate the
recycled materials
from the solvents, which can be a time-consuming and energy-intensive process.
In previous work, Marks' group at Northwestern became the first to develop catalytic processes that do not require solvents. In the new study, the team again devised a solvent-free process.
"Using solvents has many disadvantages," Kratish said. "They can be expensive, and you have to heat them up to high temperatures. Then, after the reaction, you are left with a soup of materials that you have to sort to recover the monomers. Instead of using solvents, we used water vapor from air. It's a much more elegant way to tackle plastic recycling issues."

43440321.article_summary: 北西部大学的研究人员开发了一种简单且经济的方法，利用空气中的湿气分解塑料废物。该过程使用无毒、环保的无溶剂方法，通过廉价的催化剂分解聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）的键，然后暴露在空气中，借助空气中微量的湿气将分解的PET转化为单体，这些单体是塑料的重要 building blocks。该技术比当前的塑料回收方法更安全、清洁、便宜且可持续，为创造塑料的循环经济提供了有希望的途径。该研究已发表在《Green Chemistry》上，解决了塑料废物这一全球紧迫的环境挑战。

data.title: Has the decline of knowledge work begun?
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对企业裁员、知识工作及教育的影响

不同观点：
• **Bukhmanizer** 认为，企业进行裁员的原因之一是它们减少了创新和改进工作，将希望寄托于AI，而不是继续进行大量小改进。他们的工作现在几乎只围绕一个概念：AI，且并没有详细的计划如何使用AI实现这些改进。

• **bryanlarsen** 提出相反观点，认为尽管AI提高了知识工作者的生产力，但并不意味着会减少对知识工作者的需求。通过历史对比，如服装制造业的部分自动化导致服装价格下降，需求增加，最终使得更多人从事该行业。因此，AI对知识工作者的需求可能反而会增加。

• **fullshark** 认为，大学学位体系需要彻底反思。当前的学位体系与实际技能需求脱节，导致学生背负沉重的债务，而学位并没有带来相应的工作保障或实际技能。

• **apercu** 对AI的实际效果持怀疑态度，指出当前的AI工具（如ChatGPT）在实际应用中经常出错，使用者需要具备相关知识才能识别和纠正这些错误。因此，虽然AI技术本身很了不起，但过度相信其能力是不可取的。

• **squigglydonut** 认为，如果希望AI产生更好的结果，必须对其提出高要求，仿佛生死攸关。

• **Glyptodon** 认为，知识工作的外包和低薪趋势早在AI普及之前就已经存在，AI只是加剧了这一趋势。AI的引入使得企业可以以更低成本获得尚可的结果，从而减少对高技能员工的需求。

• **7qW24A** 指出，过去10年中企业过度招聘，导致机构臃肿，而AI正好为企业提供了裁员的借口，即使AI并没有显著提升生产力，裁员也可能发生。

• **nopelynopington** 对AI在编写代码方面的能力持怀疑态度，认为即使最好的AI引擎也会写出糟糕的代码，且这种情况可能不会改善。但AI也可能让员工更容易应付工作，从而导致知识工作的整体质量下降。

• **iambateman** 认为，知识工作的技能分布广泛，大多数员工处于中等水平。AI的引入可能提升中等水平员工的能力，使得整体知识工作的平均能力上升。

• **carabiner** 指出，像机械工程等专业领域的知识工作受AI影响较小，因为这些领域的专业数据大多被企业锁住，公开数据较少，难以训练出高效的AI模型。

• **talkingtab** 提出一种更为宏观的社会经济观点，认为AI可能导致企业利润上升但同时减少对人力的需求，最终可能破坏整体经济。此外，企业擅长剥削技术红利，但可能缺乏创新动力。

• **alecco** 认为，像马斯克这样的企业已经通过AI找到了裁员的借口，许多企业可能也随之效仿，将大量工作外包至其他国家，这可能带来潜在的风险。

• **coolThingsFirst** 认为，当前就业市场竞争极其激烈，传统职业发展路径受阻，许多人开始转向小型创业公司或自谋出路。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI是否会真正减少对知识工作者的需求，或者反而会增加需求。
- 大学学位体系的可持续性及其与实际工作需求的脱节问题。
- AI在实际应用中的局限性及其可能带来的负面影响，如错误结果和低质量工作的增加。
- 企业裁员是否主要由AI驱动，或者只是企业借此机会进行结构调整。

data.title: Optimizing ML training with metagradient descent
data.author: ladberg
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种基于元梯度下降（Metagradient Descent, MGD）的方法，用于优化大规模机器学习模型的训练过程。作者提出了一种高效计算元梯度的算法，并引入了一个"平滑模型训练"框架，使得利用元梯度进行有效优化成为可能。实验表明，MGD在数据集选择和抵御数据中毒攻击方面显著优于现有方法，并且能够自动找到具有竞争力的学习率调度策略。该方法为优化模型训练配置提供了新途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于机器学习中超参数优化问题的复杂性以及对相关数学优化理论的讨论。

不同观点：
• [munchler] 认为在实际的机器学习问题中，超参数优化非常复杂且困难。每个训练运行需要很长时间，超参数之间互相影响且对硬件非常敏感，微小的配置调整可能会导致极大的性能差异。这种情况下，没有对问题领域的深入理解很难有效地搜索超参数空间。

• [jn2clark] 提出了“学习如何学习”（learning to learn）的先前工作，并询问该文章为何没有引用相关研究（如论文 https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04474）。这暗示可能存在已有文献中的方法可以用于解决当前讨论的超参数优化问题。

• [MITSardine] 对文章本身进行了深入的数学分析，指出形如 $f : x \to \text{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ 的函数通常不光滑，甚至可能不连续。此外，优化算法通常只能收敛到局部最小值，而非全局最小值。即使在数学上定义良好的情况下，数值计算中的浮点精度问题也会导致实际求解中的困难。MITSardine 还对文章中的符号和定义提出了质疑，认为文章在讨论如何正则化此类函数方面没有给出足够深入的解决方案，并提出了替代符号和定义的建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是超参数优化的实际复杂性以及是否已有其他研究（如“学习如何学习”）可以提供更好的解决方案。[munchler] 强调了实际操作中的难度，而 [jn2clark] 则指向了可能被忽视的相关研究。

• [MITSardine] 详细讨论了优化问题的数学性质，特别是函数 $f$ 的非光滑性和数值计算中的问题，并提出了对文章符号和定义的改进建议。这表明在实际应用中，理论上的优化问题比文章所讨论的更加复杂。

• 讨论中还涉及了具体的数学符号和技术细节问题，如 $\Delta_f$ 符号的使用以及定义中的技术选择，反映了在学术讨论中对精确性和符号一致性的关注。

总体而言，讨论围绕超参数优化的复杂性、已有研究的相关性以及数学优化中的理论问题展开，并包含了对文章具体内容的技术性建议。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Optimizing ML Training with Metagradient Descent, by Logan Engstrom and 5 other authors

Abstract:
A major challenge in training large-scale machine learning models is configuring the training process to maximize model performance, i.e., finding the best training setup from a vast design space. In this work, we unlock a gradient-based approach to this problem. We first introduce an algorithm for efficiently calculating metagradients -- gradients through model training -- at scale. We then introduce a "smooth model training" framework that enables effective optimization using metagradients. With metagradient descent (MGD), we greatly improve on existing dataset selection methods, outperform accuracy-degrading data poisoning attacks by an order of magnitude, and automatically find competitive learning rate schedules.

data.title: Ruby, Ractors, and lock-free data structures
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Ruby中实现并发数据结构的方法，目标是展示如何在全局可变状态下实现真正的并行处理（当前Ruby内置功能不支持）。文章涉及Ruby、Rust和C等语言，但并非必须精通。示例代码可在GitHub上找到，运行这些代码需要较新版本的Ruby（最好是可本地编译的主分支）、Rust和C编译器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby中的Ractor库的应用与挑战

不同观点：
• **Gibibit的观点**：Gibibit最初对Ractor的认知与Rust的Ractor库混淆了，他认为Rust的Ractor库非常优秀，特别是引入了Erlang/OTP的gen_server actors，值得Rust开发者关注。他对Ruby中的Ractor库文档进行了澄清。
• **Dpflan的观点**：Dpflan提到Mike Perham正在尝试利用Ractor构建可扩展的作业系统，并指出Ractor编程的难点，比如无法访问词法作用域或闭包变量，这使得Ractor编程变得复杂，甚至像是一种新的Ruby方言。他还将Ractor与Goroutines进行了类比，指出学习曲线可能类似。
• **T-writescode的观点**：T-writescode对Ractor是否真正遵循了actor模型提出疑问，尤其是邮件箱机制是否已经解决。他担心人们在使用Ractor时可能强迫actor模型遵循不合适的并行编程范式。同时，他对文章中过多提及Rust表示不解。
• **Kodablah的观点**：Kodablah提到他们的Ruby项目因使用Google Protobuf库而无法使用Ractor，因为该库不是Ractor安全的，并且无法要求用户不使用官方的Protobuf库。

补充讨论：
• **Rco8786的观点**：Rco8786认为，一个生产就绪的Ractor安全数据结构库将大大推动Ractor的采用，解决目前许多人遇到的主要障碍。

争议焦点：
• Ractor是否真正实现了actor模型，特别是邮件箱机制是否完善。
• Ractor编程的复杂性，特别是对词法作用域和闭包变量访问的限制，使得Ractor编程变得困难。
• 在Ruby项目中使用Ractor时，现有库（如Google Protobuf）的兼容性问题。

Intro
This story is about concurrent data structures in the context of Ruby. The goal here is to demonstrate how true parallelism can be achieved with global mutable state (which at the time of writing, is not supported by built-in Ruby primitives).
Familiarity with Ruby, Rust, C, (and a bit of other tooling) is nice to have, but hopefully not mandatory.
The repository with code examples can be found
on GitHub
, to run it you need a relatively new version of Ruby (master branch is probably the best option if you can compile it locally), Rust and C compilers.

data.title: Show HN: A website for sharing the "Good, Bad, and Why"s of urban spaces
data.author: kappasan
data.article_summary: 《Community Atlas of Urban Phenomena》是一个让用户分享和标记城市中各种现象的平台，用户可以根据体验将现象标记为"Good"（好）、"Bad"（坏）、"Why"（为什么）等标签，并添加评论和照片。内容涵盖设计、艺术、文化、交通、基础设施、技术、安全、健康、自然、环境、商业等多个方面。用户发布的帖子示例包括对特别建筑、城市设施、交通问题等的评价，如"1000日元卡住了"、"イベント会場へのナビゲーション"（活动会场的导航）、"マンホール周りの印"（井盖周围的标记）等。平台还提供按地区、时间、标签等筛选功能，但存在一些功能不完善的问题，如评论功能不稳定，开发者承诺在下一版本中改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个网站的功能、内容和可访问性的多方面讨论

不同观点：
• sinuhe69认为，增加自动翻译功能将使网站对更广泛的受众开放，提高可访问性。
• sgc指出，在Linux上的Firefox浏览器使用时，图片无法在详情页加载，需要借助谷歌翻译来阅读网站内容，并提供了相关页面的链接。
• cc101对网站上展示的某张海报表示不满，认为其包含种族和文化偏见的内容，并对此种内容被容忍感到不安。

补充讨论：
• ripley12对网站表示赞赏，并计划在有空时添加关于温哥华的相关条目。
• bythreads表示喜欢网站的简洁设计，并提到AI机器人可能会喜欢抓取该网站。
• chachan表达了对网站的怀旧情感，认为这是他怀念的互联网风格。
• upghost分享了自己在探索该网站时，发现了iOS的翻译功能变得更好了，并对网站开发者表示感谢。
• kappasan作为原贴作者（OP），说明了注册表单要求填写电子邮件地址只是作为用户ID使用，非有效地址也可以，但提醒如果忘记密码将无法重置。
• mc3301表示自己有空时会添加许多关于日本的相关条目。
• riffic认为网站很像"模式语言"(Pattern Language)，并希望这种网站在他所在的地区流行起来，同时提供了维基百科上关于"模式语言"的链接。

争议焦点：
• cc101提出的种族和文化偏见问题，与其他用户对网站内容的积极评价形成对比，表明在内容审核和包容性方面存在潜在争议。

43465740.article_summary: 《Community Atlas of Urban Phenomena》是一个让用户分享和标记城市中各种现象的平台，用户可以根据体验将现象标记为"Good"（好）、"Bad"（坏）、"Why"（为什么）等标签，并添加评论和照片。内容涵盖设计、艺术、文化、交通、基础设施、技术、安全、健康、自然、环境、商业等多个方面。用户发布的帖子示例包括对特别建筑、城市设施、交通问题等的评价，如"1000日元卡住了"、"イベント会場へのナビゲーション"（活动会场的导航）、"マンホール周りの印"（井盖周围的标记）等。平台还提供按地区、时间、标签等筛选功能，但存在一些功能不完善的问题，如评论功能不稳定，开发者承诺在下一版本中改进。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ghidra与LLM（大型语言模型）集成的效果和实用性

不同观点：
• mdaniel认为之前Ghidra与LLM集成的案例展示出了良好的效果，并分享了一个视频链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42860849）作为参考，显示出对这种集成持积极态度。

• Malimite提到了一篇关于iOS和macOS反编译工具的文章（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42829402），这可能暗示了在特定平台上应用此类工具的潜力，虽然未明确表态，但提供了另一个视角来审视Ghidra与LLM的结合。

• brokensegue则基于自己的经验，对直接将Ghidra内容复制到LLM并期望其自动解析的效果表示怀疑。他指出这种方法并不总是成功，并建议为这类集成工作制定一些基准以衡量效果，显示出对实际效果的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Ghidra与LLM集成在实际应用中的有效性。mdaniel看到了积极的案例，而brokensegue则基于个人经验提出了质疑，认为缺乏明确的成功标准和基准。

• 不同评论者提供了外部资源链接，为讨论提供了更多背景信息和具体案例，帮助更全面地理解Ghidra与LLM集成的应用场景和潜在问题。

• brokensegue的建议指出了一个实际问题，即在技术应用中，需要有明确的衡量标准和基准来评估新工具和方法的有效性。

data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了“休息”的概念，从俄国作家冈察洛夫的小说《奥勃洛莫夫》中的主人公对休息的看法谈起。奥勃洛莫夫认为生活的目的就是终日无所事事地躺在床上休息。文章进一步讨论了“休息”的定义，指出它不同于睡眠、 leisure（闲暇）或懒惰。作者以个人经验说明随着年龄增长，休息和睡眠变得愈发复杂和不易。文章还提到《圣经》中上帝创世后休息的例子，以及不同宗教对神圣休息日的重视，如犹太教的安息日和基督教的星期日礼拜。最后，文章指出，休息对恶人是无缘的，地狱之所以可怕部分正是因为没有休息。

43450745.article_content:
The Russian novelist Ivan Goncharov once said of writers, “And to write and write, like a wheel or a machine, tomorrow, the day after, on holidays; summer will come—and he must still be writing. When is he to stop and rest? Unfortunate man?” Goncharov was born in 1812 and died in 1891, so I am clearly not the model for the writer he was talking about—even though, my prolificacy having often been commented upon, I could otherwise well be. The eponymous hero of his novel
Oblomov
feels the same way about another character in the book who loves travel, and a second one who enjoys a lively social life, and a third who works hard in the hope of promotion. All of them are viewed by Oblomov as absurdly out of synch with life’s real purpose. This purpose, as Oblomov sees it, is to lie abed doing nothing all the days of one’s life. If
rest
may be said to have a champion, it is Oblomov, a gentleman by birth for whom “life was divided, in his opinion, into two halves: one consisted of work and boredom—these words were for him synonymous—the other of rest and peaceful good-humor.” Rest, unrelenting rest, is the name of Oblomov’s game.
“Just as there are polysyllabic words that say very little,” Georg Christoph Lichtenberg wrote, “so there are also monosyllabic words of infinite meaning.” “Rest” is one of those words, simple-sounding yet not easily defined. As a verb, rest means to “cease work or movement in order to relax, refresh oneself, or recover strength”; as a noun, “an instance or period of relaxing or ceasing to engage in strenuous or stressful activity.” Why isn’t this very helpful?
Rest is not quite synonymous with sleep, leisure, or laziness. When a man in his mid-70s or older asks another man of roughly the same age if he is “getting much,” he probably isn’t referring to sex but to sleep. Like as not, neither man is getting much sleep, for few older men I know make it through the night without having to get up two, three, or more times. Some are compelled to do so to visit the House of Commons, as Dylan Thomas called the bathroom. Others find their minds racing, or their sleep invaded by goofy dreams. I had a friend, a contemporary, who suffered the trifecta of insomnia, megalomania, and paranoia, and so spent the better parts of his nights awake, worrying about losing power he didn’t really have.
As an adolescent, I remember sleeping eight-, nine-, 10-hour periods. Now if I can do two or three hours at a stretch, I feel vaguely triumphant. Conversations with friends, though they bring much pleasure, tend toward the stimulating and so do not necessarily qualify as rest. Working out of my apartment, as I have for many years now, I often take afternoon naps, but these naps do not so much bring on a restful feeling as they ward off the inevitable fatigue of a man in his 80s.
Twenty-five years ago, I wrote an essay called “The Art of the Nap,” in which I set out my prowess at the act. What I remember about the essay today is an anecdote involving Hugh Lloyd-Jones, then regius professor of Greek at Oxford (because he was still alive, I didn’t use his name). Lloyd-Jones seemed to me in those days an Englishman to the highest power: He seemed to have 50 or 60 teeth, Himalayas of dandruff covered the shoulders of his blue blazer, and he spoke with a slight Oxbridge stammer. When I asked him if he napped, he replied, “Whenever possible.” Supine or prone? “Supine.” On couch or bed? “Bed.” Trousers on or off? “Generally off.” And for how long? “That depends,” he answered, “on when the cats get up.”
_____________
The concept of rest is as old as the Bible
.
On the seventh day, after creating the world and all that was in it, we are told that the Lord rested. Not, however, in His case, from fatigue, but to contemplate His further creations. Alain Corbin, a French scholar who has recently published a brief
History of Rest,
holds that for God, the day of rest was “a creative pause.” Later on, God tells Moses: “Speak to the sons of Israel and say, ‘You must keep my sabbaths carefully, because the sabbath is a
sign between myself and you
from generation to generation to show that it is I who sanctify you. You must keep the sabbath, then; it is to be held sacred by you.’”
Keeping the Sabbath, in Corbin’s words, is not about rest alone but “the holy nature of that rest.”
Mutatis mutandis,
Christians, who were of course initially mostly Jews, took up the notion of a holy day of rest, with theirs being Sunday. In some quarters, both religions are even now defined by their days of rest. Militant Islamists have been known to claim that “after we finish off the Saturday people, we shall finish you, the Sunday people.” Meanwhile, it is understood that there is no rest for the wicked, which is to say none in Hell, which in good part is what must make it so hellish.

data.title: RISC Architecture Really Did Change Everything
data.author: ecliptik
data.article_summary: 1995年电影《黑客》中，安吉丽娜·朱莉饰演的角色准确预言了RISC架构将改变一切。尽管当时电影不受欢迎，且很多人不理解其重要性，但如今RISC架构确实在21世纪再度改变科技，影响技术控制和未来发展。然而，大多数人仍不了解RISC是什么。文章作者参加了RISC-V峰会，描述了会议的技术性和参与者对RISC的深入了解。峰会上，RISC-V国际的CEO卡莉斯塔·雷德蒙通过将总部迁至瑞士来缓解成员对地缘政治中立性的担忧。尽管RISC-V正在改变各种设备的技术，但雷德蒙认为其故事可能不适合大肆宣传，因为大众仍对RISC缺乏认知。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对电影《Hackers》中RISC架构引用的看法以及RISC与RISC-V的区别

不同观点：
• remram：对朱莉正确发音"RISC"（发音为"risk"）表示赞赏，暗示正确发音不应被特别强调，因为这并无其他发音方式。
• phendrenad2：希望RISC-V不要再与《Hackers》这部30年前的糟糕电影联系在一起，认为这种联系令人尴尬，希望RISC-V能够摆脱这种负面关联。
• theandrewbailey：提供了一个链接，但未做具体评论。
• tetris11：认为文章的写作风格过于轻浮，难以阅读，请求提供总结。
• ChrisArchitect：作为《Hackers》电影的忠实粉丝，乐见电影被引用，但认为文章中的某些观点过于夸张。指出RISC芯片在当时并不是什么神秘技术，而是可以通过主流杂志如《Wired》或《PC Magazine》获取的信息。认为文章作者要么是显露了自己的年龄，要么是在虚构故事而非客观报道。
• tucnak：简单表达了对《Hackers》电影的喜爱，认为其永不过时。
• ksec：区分了RISC和RISC-V，认为许多人混淆了两者。并指出在过去30年中，CISC在性能计算方面取得了胜利，认为RISC应专注于嵌入式领域，呼吁停止在技术领域中基于意识形态、时尚或炒作的争论，回归工程本质。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是《Hackers》电影中对RISC架构的引用是否具有特殊意义，以及这种引用是否对RISC-V技术讨论有帮助或损害。

Incredibly, Angelina Jolie
called it. The year was 1995. Picture Jolie, short of both hair and acting experience, as a teenage hacker in
Hackers
. Not a lot of people saw this movie. Even fewer appreciated its relevance.
Hackers
was “grating,” Entertainment Weekly
huffed at the time
, for the way it embraced “the computer-kid-as-elite-rebel mystique currently being peddled by magazines like WIRED.” Thirty years later, Entertainment Weekly no longer publishes a magazine, WIRED does, and
Hackers
ranks among the foundational documents of the digital age. The last time I saw the movie, it was being projected onto the wall of a cool-kids bar down the street from my house.
But that’s not the incredible thing. The incredible thing, again, is that Jolie called it.
It.
The future. Midway through
Hackers
, she’s
watching her crush
(played by Jonny Lee Miller, whom she’d later marry in real life) type passionately on a next-gen laptop. “Has a killer refresh rate,” Miller says, breathing fast. Jolie replies: “P6 chip. Triple the speed of the Pentium.” Miller’s really worked up now. Then Jolie leans forward and, in that come-closer register soon to make her world-famous, says this: “RISC architecture is gonna change everything.”
You have to believe me when I say, one more time, that this is incredible. And what’s incredible is not just that the filmmakers knew what RISC architecture was. Or that Jolie pronounced it correctly (“risk”). Or even that Jolie’s character was right. What’s incredible is that she’s
still
right—arguably even
more
right—today. Because RISC architecture is, somehow, changing everything again, here in the 21st century. Who makes what. Who controls the future. The very soul of technology.
Everything.
And nobody’s talking about it.
And that’s probably because the vast majority of people everywhere, who use tech built on it every single day, still don’t know what in the computer-geek hell a RISC architecture even is.
Unless you’re
in
computer-geek hell, as I am, right now. I’ve just arrived at the annual international RISC-V (that’s “risk five”) summit in Santa Clara, California. Here, people don’t just know what RISC is. They also know what, oh, vector extensions and AI accelerators and matrix engines are. At the coffee bar, I overhear one guy say to another: “This is a very technical conference. This is a very technical
community
.” To which the other guy replies: “It ought to be. It ought to be.”
How to Get Computers—Before Computers Get You
Post-quantum algorithms, thermodynamic hardware, open source architectures, apocalypse-proof programming, and more: WIRED journeys to the freaky
frontiers of modern computing
.
OK, but where are the cool kids? It’s hard not to fixate on appearances at an event like this—a generic convention center, with generic coffee, in a generic town. I guess I was hoping for neon lights and pixie cuts. Instead it’s frumpy, forgettable menswear as far as the eye can see. There are 30 men for every woman, I count, as everyone gathers in the main hall for the morning presentations.
Then someone takes the stage, and she’s not just a she. She is Calista Redmond, the CEO of RISC-V International, and, Angelina Jolie be praised, she’s wearing a nifty jacket, a statement belt, and gold-and-silver … pumps? stilettos? Wait, what’s the difference? Of all the things to ask Redmond when I run into her at a happy hour later that day, that’s what I choose. She looks at me, smiles blankly, and just says, “I don’t know.”
In shame I retreat to the bar, where I decide I must redeem myself. So, cautiously, I make my way back to Redmond, who’s now deep in conversation with the chief marketing officer of a semiconductor startup. I try to impress them with a technical observation, something about RISC and AI. Redmond turns to me and says, “I thought you wanted to talk about shoes.” I assure her I’m not here to talk about what’s on the outside. I’m here to talk about what’s on the inside.
“Jason here is writing a story about RISC for WIRED,” Redmond tells the CMO. She’s not sure, frankly, that this is a great idea. Not because she isn’t a believer. In many ways, she’s
the
believer, the face of the brand. Attendees at the conference invoke her name with casual reverence:
Calista says this, Calista thinks that. And did you hear her
morning keynote
?
In fact I did. “We have fundamentally launched!” she announced, to the yelps of the business-casuals. RISC-V will transform, is transforming, machinery everywhere, she said, from cars to laptops to spaceships. If anyone doubts this, Redmond sends them the
Hackers
clip.
As CEO of RISC-V International, Calista Redmond moved the foundation’s headquarters from the US to Switzerland to allay members’ concerns about geopolitical neutrality.
Photograph: Jenna Garrett

43478237.article_summary: 1995年电影《黑客》中，安吉丽娜·朱莉饰演的角色准确预言了RISC架构将改变一切。尽管当时电影不受欢迎，且很多人不理解其重要性，但如今RISC架构确实在21世纪再度改变科技，影响技术控制和未来发展。然而，大多数人仍不了解RISC是什么。文章作者参加了RISC-V峰会，描述了会议的技术性和参与者对RISC的深入了解。峰会上，RISC-V国际的CEO卡莉斯塔·雷德蒙通过将总部迁至瑞士来缓解成员对地缘政治中立性的担忧。尽管RISC-V正在改变各种设备的技术，但雷德蒙认为其故事可能不适合大肆宣传，因为大众仍对RISC缺乏认知。

主要讨论点：对B2B和B2C商业模式的建议及其有效性

不同观点：
• [支持观点] **bob1029** 认为B2B模式相较于B2C更为简便和高效，特别是在支付和销售周期方面。他指出B2B只需要少数几个客户即可维持业务，而B2C则需要依赖大规模的市场推广如Google广告。此外，他认为在B2C中，只有通过Valve的游戏平台可能是个例外，因为该平台与开发者紧密合作。

• [质疑观点] **diebillionaires** 对博主的建议表示不满，认为这些建议仅有30%的有效性，暗示其余部分并不实用或不具备广泛适用性。

• [中立观点] **LinuxAmbulance** 对博主的建议表示认可，认为其提供了可靠的建议。

• [无关评价] **pickledoyster** 赞扬了博主的文章格式，认为其没有浪费读者时间，但未对建议内容本身作出评价。

• [反对观点] **ilrwbwrkhv** 提出相反的经验，认为不同模式的成功与否取决于创业者对项目的投入程度，而不是单纯依赖某种商业模式。他强调，即便是最疯狂和不完善的想法，只要创始人足够在意，也可能成功。

补充讨论：
• [术语疑问] **aurelien** 对博文中的"PMF"（Product-Market Fit）术语表示不解，可能暗示部分读者对某些专业术语不熟悉，建议博主进一步解释。

• [无关批评] **Rastonbury** 对博文中关于投资朋友的建议提出质疑，认为其具有单一案例偏差和事后偏见，且与原文主题无关。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于博主对B2B和B2C模式的建议是否具有广泛适用性和实际效用。支持者认为B2B模式更为简便，反对者则认为不同模式的成功更多取决于创业者的投入和具体情况。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章揭示了Instagram上一些通过AI生成、内容极为扭曲的视频正在流行并被货币化。这些视频包括如《爱探险的朵拉》脚部吃播、小猪佩奇厕所爆炸场景，以及篮球明星斯蒂芬·库里和勒布朗·詹姆斯的性暗示内容等。此类“脑残”AI视频通过引发用户的震惊和讨论，被算法推荐并广泛传播。创作者通过专门的Discord群组（如Interlink AI）分享制作指南，并通过Instagram的奖励计划获利。尽管内容令人不适，且常涉及侵权或不当主题，Instagram并未采取有效措施阻止其传播。这类视频还涉及种族歧视、暴力等敏感内容，成为平台上广泛传播的病毒式内容。

不同观点：
• DontchaKnowit：认为直接链接到Instagram内容是在帮助其获得更多关注，表示这是一种令人反感的做法。该评论者似乎对帮助Instagram平台吸引注意力持负面态度，暗示这种行为可能助长不良内容传播。

• akomtu：详细分析了Instagram上通过生成式AI和“brainrot”内容（指引发负面情绪的内容）对用户心理的潜在影响。该评论者认为，这些负面情绪的内容会让用户陷入一种扭曲的思维和情绪循环，最终可能导致心理上的负面影响。此外，该评论还预测这种内容形式未来可能演变为更具互动性的“AI灵魂杀手”应用，暗示科技与内容结合可能带来更大的问题。

• 争议的焦点在于是否应该通过分享链接或截图来传播Instagram上的负面内容。DontchaKnowit认为直接分享链接是在帮助这些内容获得更多关注，而OgsyedIE则提供了一种避免直接链接的方法。
• akomtu进一步探讨了这些内容对用户心理的深层次影响，特别是通过生成式AI技术，可能会导致用户陷入负面的情绪循环，甚至未来演变为更复杂的交互式负面内容。
• 总体来看，讨论的核心是如何负责任地处理和分享社交媒体上的负面内容，以及这些内容对用户心理健康的潜在危害。

'Brainrot' AI on Instagram Is Monetizing the Most Fucked Up Things You Can Imagine (and Lots You Can't)
Jason Koebler

at 12:59 PM
The hottest use of AI right now? Dora the Explorer feet mukbang; Peppa the Pig Skibidi toilet explosion; Steph Curry and LeBron James Ahegao Drakedom threesome.
This article contains potentially disturbing graphics and descriptions that are nonetheless viral on Instagram and other major platforms.
These are words I never thought I would type, and the people in my life who I have said them to have told me to immediately stop speaking. But here is how I would describe the type of AI generated reels that are popular on Instagram right now:
Dora the Explorer feet mukbang
;
Peppa the Pig Skibidi toilet explosion
; Steph Curry and LeBron James
Ahegao Drakedom threesome
;
LeBron James and Diddy raping Steph Curry in prison
;
anthropomorphic fried egg strippers
;
iPhone case made of human skin
; any number of sexualized Disney princesses doing anything you can imagine and lots of things you can’t;
mermaids making out with fish
;
demon monster eating a woman’s head
; face-swapped
AI adult influencers with Down syndrome
, and,
unfortunately, this
. Unfortunately, I swear to you that the screengrabs and videos I am including and linking to in this article are not the worst that I have seen on Instagram.
Other “niches” that have become popular on Instagram and which have begun to regularly pop up on my feed are wildly racist AI videos of Black men whose faces are put on dogs or gorillas, Black men storming KFC restaurants and chasing after watermelon, George Floyd opening a “Fent-Donalds,” Martin Luther King Jr. in a tub of green sludge, Anne Frank as a zionist cyborg, etc.
As I wrote last week
, the strategy with these types of posts is to make a human linger on them long enough to say to themselves “what the fuck,” or to be so horrified as to comment “what the fuck,” or send it to a friend saying “what the fuck,” all of which are signals to the algorithm that it should boost this type of content but are decidedly not signals that the average person actually wants to see this type of thing. The type of content that I am seeing right now makes “
Elsagate
,” the YouTube scandal in which disturbing videos were targeted to kids and resulted in various YouTube reforms, look quaint.
“Brainrot” and creepypasta AI-generated reels are currently some of the most popular metas, or hyper-specific niches of content being made by the community of people who are creating and monetizing AI slop en masse.
I was able to find the creators of some of the viral brainrot Instagram reels I described above discussing their process for making them on a Discord called Interlink AI, which costs $30 to join and comes with guides to making AI reels. The Discord has specific guides for “brainrot” videos, “realistic” videos, and “pov” videos. As we have reported before, the creation of AI slop is very mechanical and replicable, which is why we see so much of it. Once a method for going viral is discovered, the person who discovered it often makes guides that they then advertise and sell, and other people in the community then begin copying them.
Instagram, of course, is doing nothing to stop the spread of this type of AI, and the Discord tells users that one of the best ways to make money from this type of AI is
through Instagram’s Bonus program
which offers “direct payouts.” This type of content is most popular on Instagram, but is also on YouTube and TikTok, though, anecdotally, it does not seem to perform nearly as well there. The Interlink Discord also warns people not to post real people or copyrighted characters to TikTok: "Steer clear of using protected characters or content that could violate intellectual property rights, such as popular TV or movie figures (like SpongeBob)."

• akomtu进一步探讨了这些内容对用户心理的深层次影响，特别是通过生成式AI技术，可能会导致用户陷入负面的情绪循环，甚至未来演变为更复杂的交互式负面内容。
• 总体来看，讨论的核心是如何负责任地处理和分享社交媒体上的负面内容，以及这些内容对用户心理健康的潜在危害。

data.author: lawik
data.article_summary: Cyanview是一家比利时小公司，专注于为现场视频广播行业提供色彩调节产品，确保大型活动如超级碗中多达200台摄像机的视觉一致性。其远程控制面板（RCP）已成为行业标准，应用于奥运会、超级碗、NBA等顶级赛事。Cyanview选择使用Elixir编程语言，因其卓越的网络功能和弹性，能够可靠地协调大量设备。Elixir帮助Cyanview解决了与多种摄像机和视频设备的集成问题，尤其是在远程制作场景下，如跨洲控制摄像机。该公司通过大量逆向工程，确保其产品兼容各种专业摄像系统，并提供API以实现与其他设备的顺畅集成。在一次北京奥运会项目中，Cyanview设备成功解决了Panasonic PTZ摄像机的远程控制问题，展示了其系统的可靠性。

   - **brcmthrowaway**：对Elixir是否在实时访问色彩像素数据提出疑问。

补充讨论：

Cyanview: Coordinating Super Bowl's visual fidelity with Elixir
March 25, 2025 · by Lars Wikman, José Valim · in
Elixir in Production
How do you coordinate visual fidelity across two hundred cameras for a live event like the Super Bowl?
The answer is: by using the craft of camera shading, which involves adjusting each camera to ensure they match up in color, exposure and various other visual aspects. The goal is to turn the live event broadcast into a cohesive and consistent experience. For every angle used, you want the same green grass and the same skin tones. Everything needs to be very closely tuned across a diverse set of products and brands. From large broadcast cameras, drone cameras, and PTZ cameras to gimbal-held mirrorless cameras and more. This is what Cyanview does. Cyanview is a small Belgian company that sells products for the live video broadcast industry, and its primary focus is shading.
Broadcast is a business where you only get one chance to prove that your tool is up to the task. Reliability is king. There can be no hard failures.
A small team of three built a product so powerful and effective that it spread across the industry purely on the strength of its functionality. Without any marketing, it earned a reputation among seasoned professionals and became a staple at the world’s top live events. Cyanview’s Remote Control Panel (RCP) is now used by specialist video operators on the Olympics, Super Bowl, NFL, NBA, ESPN, Amazon and many more. Even most fashion shows in Paris use Cyanview’s devices.
These devices put Elixir right in the critical path for serious broadcast operations. By choosing Elixir, Cyanview gained best-in-class networking features, state-of-the-art resilience and an ecosystem that allowed fast iteration on product features.
Why Elixir?
The founding team of Cyanview primarily had experience with embedded development, and the devices they produce involve a lot of low-level C code and plenty of FPGA. This is due to the low-level details of color science and the really tight timing requirements.
If you’ve ever worked with camera software, you know it can be a mixed bag. Even after going fully digital, much of it remained tied to analog systems or relied on proprietary connectivity solutions. Cyanview has been targeting IP (as in Internet Protocol) from early on. This means Cyanview’s software can operate on commodity networks that work in well-known and well-understood ways. This has aligned well with an increase in remote production, partially due to the pandemic, where production crews operate from a central location with minimal crew on location. Custom radio frequency or serial wire protocols have a hard time scaling to cross-continent distances.
This also paved the way for Elixir, as the Erlang VM was designed to communicate and coordinate millions of devices, reliably, over the network.
Elixir was brought in by the developer Ghislain, who needed to build integrations with cameras and interact with the other bits of required video gear, with many different protocols over the network. The language comes with a lot of practical features for encoding and decoding binary data down to the individual bits. Elixir gave them a strong foundation and the tools to iterate fast.
Ghislain has been building the core intellectual property of Cyanview ever since. While the physical device naturally has to be solid, reliable, and of high quality, a lot of the secret sauce ultimately lies in the massive number of integrations and huge amounts of reverse engineering. Thus, the product is able to work with as many professional camera systems and related equipment as possible. It is designed to be compatible with everything and anything a customer is using. Plus, it offers an API to ensure smooth integration with other devices.
David Bourgeois, the founder of Cyanview, told us a story how these technical decisions alongside Elixir helped them tackle real-world challenges:
“During the Olympics in China, a studio in Beijing relied on a large number of Panasonic PTZ cameras. Most of their team, however, was based in Paris and needed to control the cameras remotely to run various shows throughout the day. The problem? Panasonic’s camera protocols were never designed for internet use — they require precise timing and multiple messages for every adjustment. With network latency, that leads to timeouts, disconnects, and system failures… So they ended up placing our devices next to the cameras in Beijing and controlled them over IP from Paris — just as designed.”
The devices in a given location communicate and coordinate on the network over a custom MQTT protocol. Over a hundred cameras without issue on a single Remote Control Panel (RCP), implemented on top of Elixir’s network stack.
Technical composition

data.author: 1sembiyan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Intel RealSense深度摄像头系列，包括入门级的D421模块以及其他多种型号（如D456、D457、D455f、D435、D415等），每款摄像头具有不同的视野、理想距离和功能特点，如全局快门、IMU和IP67防水防尘等级。文章还展示了这些摄像头在辅助视障人士（.lumen眼镜）、安全筛查（Thruvision）、店内运营自动化（Simbe Robotics）和工业检测自动化（ANYBotics）等领域的应用案例。此外，文章提供了SDK 2.0、文档、代码示例和教程等开发资源，并支持多种编程语言和操作系统。用户可以根据需求选择最合适的摄像头，并通过线上或授权经销商购买。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Intel RealSense及其替代产品的使用体验与技术优劣

不同观点：
• Uehreka：因Intel对RealSense产品线的不确定性（如团队裁员或停产传闻），选择了Stereolabs的ZED 2i。认为ZED 2i功能良好，但垂直安装时骨骼追踪效果不佳。同时，肯定了Stereolabs的软件更新速度。
• Symmetry：回顾了Kinect和RealSense的历史，指出Intel曾填补Kinect退出后的市场空缺，但近期关于RealSense的停产声明引发了业界恐慌，促使一些公司开发内部3D传感器系统。不过，Intel将RealSense独立出来，可能避免了彻底关闭。
• IshKebab：误以为Intel早已关闭RealSense，但发现D421模块仍是新产品，并认为其价格合理，期待更小批量销售。
• ftrobro：曾尝试RealSense但结果不可靠，推荐使用Chronoptics KEA，效果更好。
• donatj：质疑RealSense是否已停产，并讨论其硬件是否承担立体图像解码功能，或完全依赖软件处理。
• omershapira：指出这些传感器虽利润微薄但行业必需，易受企业高管成本优化影响，导致行业倒退。
• aomix：通过更换为D457型号解决了USB版本的可靠性问题，对结果满意。
• sand500：询问RealSense是否会取代Xbox Kinects。
• londons_explore：指出全球快门相机的下一代通常会使用卷帘快门以降低成本，并提高性能。
• momoschili：认为RealSense自2016年以来未有重大突破，可能被ToF或LIDAR技术取代，仅在特定工业或爱好领域有应用。
• phkahler：质疑RealSense的测距范围参数不一致，存在矛盾。
• johnmarie：推荐使用Zivid相机，认为其工业级质量和结构光技术更优，尽管价格更高。
• ycuser2：询问是否可以用RealSense拍摄180°的3D视频。

补充讨论：
• 对RealSense产品线未来发展的担忧和不确定性是讨论的焦点，尤其是关于其是否停产及独立运营的问题。
• 不同用户对RealSense的可靠性和功能性有不同评价，一些人推荐了替代产品如ZED 2i、Chronoptics KEA和Zivid。
• 技术细节如USB传输的脆弱性、快门类型、测距范围等问题也被深入讨论。
• 有对价格和硬件功能的质疑，尤其是与其他新兴技术（如ToF和LIDAR）的比较。

争议焦点：
• Intel RealSense是否已停产及其未来发展方向的不确定性。
• RealSense与其他替代产品（如ZED 2i和Chronoptics KEA）的性能和可靠性比较。
• 技术参数（如测距范围）的不一致性。

43447819.article_content:
What’s the difference between an en dash and em dash?
There are hyphens. Then there are dashes. There’s the en dash. Then there’s the em dash.
And these diddy lines can cause all sorts of confusion when you’re writing your marketing copy. If you spot them at all.
At a glance, you might not notice the difference between these three punctuation marks. And even if you do, they’re not the easiest things to add in when you actually want to use them.
So let’s break down the difference between an en dash and an em dash. And I’ll tell you exactly where you can find them.
A fine line
Let’s rule out the smallest of the three marks.
Here’s the hyphen: /-/
It’s used to create a compound word. It gathers two words together and snuggles them in without any spaces. We need these so there’s no uncertainty and confusion in meaning.
Compare these...
Is Brenda living her best life with some
extra marital sex
? Lucky Bernadette! After eight years together they’re gearing things back up.
Or is Brenda having
extra-marital sex
? I bet it’s with Tabitha. From book club. Tut.
We’re not looking at these here. So head over to
how to use hyphens
for the ins and outs
Cut a dash
Now onto the dashes.
Here’s the en dash: /–/
It’s the width of an ‘n’ and it shows an inclusive range. A ‘from and to’ situation. And there are no spaces.
Rule 1
: Book club was 7
–
10pm.
You don’t use ‘from’ or ‘between’ with an en dash. If you want to use it then you need a ‘to’ between the range instead. Like this…
Rule 2
: Book club ran
from
7pm
to
10pm.
And this is the em dash: /—/
Unsurprisingly, it’s around the width of an ‘m’ and there are no spaces either side either. Here are the three ways you’ll most likely use it.
Rule 1
: When more emphasis is needed than a pair of commas, or just like a pair of brackets. We don't use this so much in UK English now. I'll fill you in on that later.
Book club
—
more like wine club
—
was every Wednesday night.
Rule 2
: An aside or afterthought.
Last week’s book was Tipping the Velvet
—
she preferred Fingersmith.
Rule 3
: A sudden break in speech.
“But Tabitha is just a
—
"
BUT…
In the UK, we tend to have ditched the em dash unless it’s for punctuating speech. Instead, we use the en dash with a space either side. It’s easier on the eye. You can use them to replace the en dash in rules 1 and 2 above. Like this…
Book club
–
more like wine club
–
was every Wednesday night.
Last week’s book was Tipping the Velvet
–
she preferred Fingersmith.
Slapdash
When we use Word it tries to make it easy for you to type the symbol you need. From now on, anything in forward slashes is what you need to key in. Don’t type the //.
Here’s what to type:
►
En dash: /number space hyphen space number/ so /1999
-
2001/ to get /1999
–
2001/
►
Em dash: /word hyphen hyphen word/ so /word
--
word/ to get /word
—
word/
BUT…
that date range is wrong.
The ‘from and to’ ranges that use an en dash with numbers shouldn’t have a space either side of them. This autotyping in Word works well if we want to use an en dash with a space either side, like brackets. But not for ranges.
Keep an eye on what Word’s up to without you realising as you type.
Take a shortcut
You can type shortcuts so you don’t even need to look up from your screen. Make sure you have Number Lock switched on and use these keystrokes:
►
En dash: /Ctrl+Minus/ and /Alt+0150/
►
Em dash: /Ctrl+Alt+Minus/ and /Alt+0151/
But are you really going to remember those codes? I sure don’t.
And if you have a laptop that doesn’t have a number keypad on the right of the keyboard then it doesn’t even work.
It’s easier to insert the symbol manually. Then copy and paste if you need it again. Here’s how…
Choose your character
Head up to
Insert
on the toolbar. Click
Symbol
in Word or
Special Characters
in Google Docs. Look for the dashes.
It’s not always easy to tell which dash is which. If you hover over or click on it then it’ll tell you:
►
En dash: symbol #45 or unicode /U+2013/
►
Em dash: symbol #190 or unicode /U+2014/
Work it on the web
If you’re writing for the web, you DO need to type in a code to get your dashes. (There isn’t at the time of writing, but that might change). Instead, you need to write your copy in HTML or markdown and use these codes:
En dash: /–/ or /–/
Em dash: /—/ or /—/
(I know, I know, the bullets are inconsistent. The markdown text box I’ve used so far in this article converts the keystrokes to the symbols, so I’ve had to use a basic text box to spell them out for you.)
Oh, dash it!
What if you don’t want to mess with HTML or add markdown blocks to your webpage?
Don’t if you don’t want to.
I hardly use them for the web these days as it’s more effort. I use punchier sentences instead. And I’ve developed my writing style from it.
You can’t type dashes straight into social media posts either. You can copy and paste them. But, really? It’s a lot of faffing around for something we consume and scroll past so quickly.
So don’t do that either if you don’t want to.

data.title: Evolving Scala
data.author: pjmlp
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Scala语言的未来发展方向，强调了持续创新的必要性。尽管Scala的热度已不如2010年代，但它在技术上比十年前更加成熟，拥有更稳固的基础和更广泛的生态系统。文章指出，Scala的核心价值在于结合了**安全**和**便利**，以及面向对象与函数式编程的融合。然而，随着其他语言的进步，Scala必须在保持优势的同时，解决其弱点，特别是在新手入门体验上进行改进。

未来，Scala的开发重点将包括：在**不牺牲便利**的前提下提高**安全性**，如引入捕获检查、显式空值、安全初始化等功能；以及在**保证安全**的前提下增加**便利**，如引入枚举、可选括号、命名元组等。文章还提到，数据字面量聚合的讨论正在进行中，但尚未有定论。Scala需要不断前进，以保持其吸引力和相关性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Scala 编程语言的现状、优缺点以及其未来发展。

不同观点：
• epolanski 认为 Scala 3 的开发者不断添加新功能，导致工具和社区难以跟上。他主张停止开发新功能，专注于现有生态系统，因为当前语言已经非常优秀。他还指出，Scala 作为学术研究项目的一部分，开发者往往忽视社区的反馈。
• nikitaga 持积极态度，认为 Scala 非常享受和高效，特别是在团队开发中。虽然 Scala 2 到 Scala 3 的过渡期有些艰难，但现在使用 Scala 3 非常顺利，语言和生态系统都在向好的方向发展。

• Scala 的功能丰富和强大与其复杂性和社区分裂的争议并存。

• Scala 在函数式编程和并发处理方面的独特优势与其他语言的赶超对比。
• Scala 在实际项目中的成功应用与在更广泛行业中应用的局限性。

争议焦点：Scala 是否应继续开发新功能，还是应专注于现有生态系统的完善和普及。

43468972.article_content:
Evolving Scala
Monday 24 March 2025
Martin Odersky and Haoyi Li
BLOG
There is always ongoing discussion about the future direction of the Scala language.
How fast should it move?
What needs to be improved?
Should the language change at all?
This article discusses how
Scala must keep evolving
, why that evolution is necessary, and what directions we expect that evolution to take.
We hope that this will cover many of the frequently asked questions on the direction of the Scala language, and help the community understand where the language will go in the months and years to come.
Summary
Although Scala is no longer riding the wave of hype it had in the mid-2010s, by most surveys the language maintains its position just outside the list of mainstream languages.
From a technical perspective, the core language and ecosystem have improved greatly over the past decade.
In many ways Scala is on much better foundations today than it was 10 years ago.
Scala has a history of leading the way for the rest of the programming field.
In exchange for a bit less polish and stability than mainstream languages, people chose Scala to get next decadeâs language features today.
The value of Scala has always been the unique combination of
safety
and
convenience
that these language features have enabled, and its fusion of
object oriented
and
functional
programming ideas that can elegantly accommodate these features.
But other languages are also improving, and so Scala must continue to innovate, improving on both its strengths and weaknesses with a particular focus on the newcomer onboarding experience.
There are of course ongoing issues, especially around IDE support and the learnability of the ecosystem, and there will always be concerns about tooling, compatibility, and migration cost as a language evolves.
But Scala has no choice but to move forward if it is to maintain its appeal and relevance in the years to come.
Where Scala stands today
Although the hype has died down, popularity-wise Scala is about where it has always been: not quite in the mainstream, but with far greater adoption than more niche languages.
For example, the RedMonk Language Rankings had Scala in
14th place in 2014
and
still in 14th place 10 years later in 2024
.
In those years, the programming landscape changed significantly: Swift replacing Objective C, the emergence of Go and Kotlin and Dart and Rust, the decline of CoffeeScript and Perl.
Yet throughout this Scalaâs place remains unchanged.
Although individuals in the community come and go, Scala as a whole seems to be holding strong with a solid base of enthusiasts.
Technically, Scala is on stronger foundations than it was 10 years ago.
The ecosystem has matured and the various Reactive or Pure-FP styles have found their audiences.
Alternative styles like the
Scala Toolkit
and the
com.lihaoyi
platform are now available.
New build tools like
Scala-CLI
and
Mill
have emerged, and developer tools like
Scalafmt
and
Scalafix
have become widely used.
IDEs remain a pain point, but we expect them to improve over the course of 2025.
Heavy use of symbolic operators has thankfully fallen out of style.
Scala has always been a language on the leading edge, proving the viability of language features like lambdas, records, and pattern matching that were adopted 10â15 years later by Java, Python, and other mainstream languages.
It remains to be seen which current Scala features the mainstream languages will adopt 10-15 years from now.
Where is Scala going?
In this section, we will discuss some areas where the core Scala developers will focus their efforts.
Safety and convenience: pick two
Scala has always been a hybrid language.
The fusion of object-oriented and functional styles was often talked about.
But its other fusion has been of
safety
and
convenience.
Traditionally, âscriptingâ languages like Python were unsafe but convenient, while âapplicationâ languages like Java were safe but inconvenient.
Scala was the first to prove that you can do both in the same language.
More modern languages like Swift or Kotlin have progressed in this direction as well, the idea was unheard of when Scala first started.
However, the programming landscape has not stood still for the last two decades.
Much of what used to be unique to Scala is now common.
All modern languages provide generics, type inference, lambdas, records, pattern matching, and other such features.
To continue to attract users, Scala must continue to innovate in both directions:
Increasing safety
without compromising convenience: features like
capture checking
,
explicit nulls
,
safe initialization
,
multiversal equality
.
Increasing convenience
without compromising safety: features like
enums
,
optional braces
,
named tuples
.
A discussion about
aggregate data literals
has sparked a lot of interest, although it is still too early to see what will come out of it.
The Scala ecosystem is broad and diverse, but we think these twin goals are the common thre
43468972.article_summary:
本文讨论了Scala语言的未来发展方向，强调了持续创新的必要性。尽管Scala的热度已不如2010年代，但它在技术上比十年前更加成熟，拥有更稳固的基础和更广泛的生态系统。文章指出，Scala的核心价值在于结合了**安全**和**便利**，以及面向对象与函数式编程的融合。然而，随着其他语言的进步，Scala必须在保持优势的同时，解决其弱点，特别是在新手入门体验上进行改进。

未来，Scala的开发重点将包括：在**不牺牲便利**的前提下提高**安全性**，如引入捕获检查、显式空值、安全初始化等功能；以及在**保证安全**的前提下增加**便利**，如引入枚举、可选括号、命名元组等。文章还提到，数据字面量聚合的讨论正在进行中，但尚未有定论。Scala需要不断前进，以保持其吸引力和相关性。

data.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro reasons about task feasibility
data.author: intellectronica
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者尝试使用AI模型Gemini 2.5 Pro创建一个虚拟合成器，目标是重现90年代末的ReBirth RB-338合成器。然而，AI经过分析后认为该任务过于复杂，无法一次性完成，并详细解释了原因，包括项目所需的专业知识和开发时间。不同于一般AI的失败尝试，Gemini主动停止了任务，并建议提供一个简化的概念起点，包括基本代码和UI元素。经过协商，AI最终生成了一个简化但可运行的合成器。这一行为展示了AI在判断任务可行性方面的进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在处理复杂任务、生成创意内容及面对无法直接解决的问题时的表现和潜力

不同观点：
• **SimonW**：分享了自己使用Gemini 2.5 Pro处理复杂编码任务的积极体验，并提供了具体例子，但也提到在公开平台分享这类成果存在被质疑的风险，如例子可能被认为是 trivial 或不现实的。
• **Tkgally**：受SimonW的启发，展示了Gemini 2.5 Pro生成音乐合成器的成果，并详细描述了生成过程和推理路径，强调了模型在创造性和意外性方面的潜力。
• **Wiz21c**：指出LLM与传统程序不同，由于输入空间巨大，用户难以完全探索其功能，因此LLM可以在很长一段时间内带来惊喜。
• **Jrvarela56**：提出未来LLM可以分解复杂请求为可处理的子请求，通过协调多个子组件来解决问题，并认为这是构建AGI（人工通用智能）的关键。
• **Ofirtwo**：关注LLM在无法通过参考用户解决智力任务时的表现，希望模型能深入探索问题并最终承认无法解答，而不是立即将问题抛回给用户。
• **Coolgoose**：幽默地建议下一步是教会LLM拖延。
• **Retrofuturism**：质疑某些任务被拒绝是否仅仅是由于系统提示决定了这些请求可能会消耗过多资源并导致失败。
• **Menzoic**：分享了GPT-4在零 shot 提示下进行类似“谈判”的经历，模型通过迭代方法继续任务。
• **Vladmdgolam**：提到在使用o1-pro生成回文时，模型会识别不可能的情况并给出具体例子。

补充讨论：
• **Trash_cat**：对输入提示的具体内容表示好奇，暗示提示的设计可能对结果有重要影响。

争议焦点：
• 对LLM生成结果的原创性和意外性的评价存在分歧，部分人认为模型可能只是重复已有知识（如StackOverflow上的内容），而其他人则强调其创造性和潜力。
• 关于LLM面对无法解决的问题时应如何表现，存在不同期待，部分人希望模型能深入探索并最终承认无法解答，而不是简单地将问题抛回用户。

Negotiating with the Machine
... in which a surprisingly reflective AI tells me no (for good reasons) ...

After spending some time this morning generating various pictures of monkeys I got bored and decided to ask Gemini 2.5 Pro to create a virtual synthesizer for me. My initial ambition was to get a recreation of the famous ReBirth RB-338 virtual synth from the late 90s, and I have gathered a pretty good spec and instructed the AI to recreate it in HTML and Javascript.
What happened next is surprising and significant. Gemini did its “thinking” schtick. During its thinking session it reached the conclusion that this task is not feasible in one shot. It then stopped and explained that to me.
Thinking Excerpt:
…
Feasibility Assessment:
Creating a complete and fully working reproduction of ReBirth RB-338 is an enormous undertaking, likely requiring months or even years of development by an experienced team. It involves deep knowledge of digital signal processing (DSP), web audio APIs (like Tone.js), UI development, and the specific nuances of the original hardware ReBirth emulated.
Limitations:
Complexity: The scope is far beyond what can be generated in a single response. It's a full-scale software development project.
Accuracy: Achieving authentic emulation, especially for the TB-303 filter, is extremely challenging. Tone.js provides building blocks, but the specific tuning and interaction of components require significant DSP expertise.
…
Conclusion: It is not feasible to generate a complete, fully working reproduction of ReBirth RB-338 as requested in a single response. The complexity and scope are too large.
Alternative Approach:
I can provide a basic structural outline and some simplified example code snippets demonstrating key concepts using HTML, JavaScript, and Tone.js to illustrate how one might start building such a project. This would include:
Basic HTML structure.
Setting up Tone.js.
A very simplified representation of one TB-303-style synth with a few controls (e.g., cutoff, resonance).
A very simplified 16-step sequencer.
Basic UI elements (e.g., simple buttons/sliders).
This will not be a ReBirth clone, but rather a conceptual starting point.
…
I have never seen an LLM do this. Typically, if I request something that can’t be achieved, the AI will just try and fail miserably. Gemini 2.5 Pro’s ability to reason about what it can and cannot do is a powerful and important new type of behaviour.
Anyway, not one to take no for an answer, I negotiated, and Gemini did produce a simpler but nevertheless fully working and fun synthesizer.
Give it a try
.

data.title: All clothing is handmade (2022)
data.author: panic
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了手工制作服装的特殊价值以及对成衣质量的误解。作者讲述了自己制作被子和衣服的经历，强调了定制服装的情感联系。文章指出，所有服装本质上都是手工制作的，无论是在家中自制还是工厂生产。作者批评了人们对廉价成衣质量的偏见，尤其是对来自某些国家的服装。文章解释，成衣质量的好坏取决于品牌在材料选择、剪裁、设计和生产速度等方面的决策，而非生产地工人的技能。文章最后质疑了对东亚国家服装生产能力的刻板印象，呼吁重新思考我们对成衣质量和生产者的评价方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：服装质量、生产外包、手工与量产之间的质量差异以及通货膨胀对商品质量的影响。

不同观点：
• **量产服装质量下降与通胀关系**：alabastervlog认为，自1970年代以来，经济进步的表象实际上是商品质量下降的结果，尤其是服装。例如，现代18美元的衬衫质量远不如1940年代或1950年代的同类产品。这种质量下降导致实际通胀率被低估。

• **手工与量产的质量差异**：andrewvc指出，手工制作的皮具（如钱包）质量往往优于量产品，因为手工制作者可以选择更高质量的材料，且不追求量产的效率。然而，量产涉及的工业缝纫技术仍然需要高度熟练的工人操作，且量产设计更注重外观而非耐用性。

• **自制服装的满足感与成本**：squeedles分享了自己制作服装的经验，认为自制服装不仅能满足个人需求，还能提供创造性满足。然而，制作一件高质量衬衫需要大量时间，难以规模化生产，这也解释了量产服装为何通过降低成本来提高利润。

• **现代内衣质量下降**：fifticon提到现代男性内衣质量下降，尤其是弹性材料部分，使用寿命明显缩短，怀疑是企业为了促进重复购买而故意设计的。

争议焦点：
• **商品质量下降的原因**：一部分评论者（如alabastervlog和blululu）认为商品质量下降是企业为了追求利润而故意降低成本的结果，而另一些人（如andrewvc）则认为这是生产规模化和设计选择的结果。

43450515.article_content:
All Clothing Is Handmade
2022-10-29
quilts
The idea for this quilt came to me several years ago. Besides making quilts, I make some of my own clothes and occasionally make clothes for people in my life. I made my own wedding dress and one for a college friend as well (and never doing that again).
There’s something special nowadays about something that was made or tailored just for you, whether it was done by a friend/family member or something you had made. When I was a kid, my father gave my mother a birthday gift of what was essentially a copy of her favorite dress, made by a local seamstress. The style was pretty basic, but not being sold in stores at that time. I’m sure it was quite expensive. It was very thoughtful, she loved and wore the dress for ages, until her cancer surgeries made its fit uncomfortable.
But while I love the personal connections of bespoke/self-made clothing, I want to push back a bit against some language that occurs when people (myself included) talk about store-bought clothing, especially cheaper clothing. Whether it’s the nice Lands End flannel shirt I’m wearing as I write this, or the one my husband is wearing that I made for him, or the TikTok influencer’s Shein t-shirt that rips when she tries it on… all clothing is handmade.
I made this quilt using worn textiles from friends, family, and some folks in my church and scraps from my own projects. It’s got a piece of fabric from my wedding dress and others from one of my mom’s favorite dresses. There’s a couple of my husband’s old dress shirts, bits of my father’s ties, the lining of my little sister’s worn jacket, highlights from a friend’s tunic, bits of baby dresses, another friend’s dress shirt, and more. There’s a couple little pieces of leftover fabric from that same flannel shirt my husband is wearing right now.
I pieced it ages ago, I can’t quite even remember… 2020? It’s a wonky quilt, dozens of fabrics that were never meant to sit side-by-side. A little leather just for fun and frustration. It took forever to figure out how I wanted to quilt it (large stitches with long strokes, colors matching as best I could in the blocks themselves) and then to get to it, but I’m very glad that it’s done and I can share it now.
Who Controls Clothing’s Quality
21st century textile production happens on a massive scale, one that keeps ramping up and has enormous environmental costs. The quality of mass-market textiles has dropped noticeably since the 1990s, which were also a noticeable drop from the 1970s.
When people talk about this change in quality, the language often carries a set of assumptions. These assumptions are often both geographically and racially coded. “This t-shirt was made in Honduras” or “This blouse was made in Cambodia” imply things about their quality and often subtly, sometimes not-so-subtly, attached to the people actually doing the work.
But even if one assessed ten thousand blouses made in Cambodia for their quality, any negative findings say nothing about the talents or potential of Cambodian garment workers as a whole or relate to, say, American garment workers. What they reflect instead are:
The brand’s choice of materials:
Where did the cloth come from and how was it made?
What kind of thread are they using? (Thread can make a major difference in the longevity of a garment. The recent trend of lowering thread quality to save money is why the crotch of your new pants split after a month when the last pair you got of these same pants lasted a solid 5 years.)
The cutting setup:
How many layers of fabric are being cut together?
How much time do the workers have to operate cutting tools?
How likely are things to slip and slide during the cutting process?
The actual garment design. Before a garment is made, especially in a mass-production context, decisions about construction need to be made including:
How are the seams finished?
What’s the stitch length?
How are buttons attached?
The speed at which it is being made:
Is the garment worker sewing 30 seams an hour? 60? 100?
What happens when there’s an error?
What kind of breaks does the worker get? Really?
These decisions are all made by the company that ordered the clothing and, quite possibly, also by one or more subcontractors. While brands may plead innocence and outsourcing, the cost per item they demand from their suppliers directly influences this…and they know it.
Mass-produced clothing is low quality when someone
overseeing the project
decided to make it low quality. Mass-produced clothing is high quality when someone
overseeing the project
decided to make it high quality. What country it came from and who made it is a reflection of how the company wanted to pay and treat the people making it, not of those people’s skills or potential.
How does the way we speak of textile manufacturing (especially that done in East Asia) create and reinforce perceptions of East Asian women’s (primarily in our perception) capacity to do high-quality sewing? Why do we let

data.title: How to protect your phone and data privacy at the US border
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了如何在美国边境保护手机和数据隐私。由于宪法在边境地区的保护较弱，美国海关和边境保护局（CBP）可以检查你的设备，包括手机。为降低风险，专家建议：

1. **决定是否配合检查**：提前考虑是否愿意在入境时解锁手机。拒绝可能导致设备被没收或更长时间的盘查。
2. **关闭手机和面部识别**：入境前关闭手机和面部识别功能。
3. **不要擦除手机数据**：这可能引起怀疑。
4. **加密数据并使用强密码**：增加破解难度。
5. **将数据移至云存储**：减少本地存储的敏感信息。

每个人的风险评估不同，取决于移民身份、旅行历史和手机数据敏感性。提前准备可以有效保护隐私。

主要讨论点：美国边境数据隐私与安全问题，以及应对措施

不同观点：
• Latexr：担心无故被拘留的风险比数据隐私更大，建议不要前往美国，因为美国传达了不欢迎外来者的信号。
• Surac：将数据从手机转移到云端实际上还是将数据交给了美国，因为云服务仍在美国控制下。
• Btbuildem：提到有人因线上活动（如社交媒体帖子）被拘留，建议删除不常用的社交媒体账户，并质疑主要社交平台是否保留长期的删除记录供政府访问。
• Havoc：建议在"可疑国家"使用一次性手机，但认为即便如此，美国政府可能仍通过云端获取数据。

• Londons_explore：提出将手机邮寄到美国，到达时使用一次性手机或不带手机，以避免数据被检查。

• Hoseja：讽刺英国人也提出类似观点。
• Mschuster91：建议欧盟、印度和中国对美国旅客实施类似措施，以让美国国会意识到问题严重性。

• 争议焦点在于美国边境搜查和数据隐私的实际风险，部分人认为风险被夸大，而其他人则建议采取极端措施规避风险。
• 讨论中反复提到云存储和数据隐私的关系，以及如何在旅行时保护个人数据的不同策略。
